title: Foreign-currency borrowing would change how Sweden funds its reserves
summary: The Riksbank plans to borrow roughly SEK 200 billion in foreign currency through the Swedish National Debt Office. Its 4 November release gives the objective as reducing the balance sheet’s sensitivity to the krona, while preserving the long-term size of the foreign-currency reserve. The proposal could generate purchases of kronor, which makes it relevant to currency markets even though the bank explicitly assigned it no monetary policy purpose.

The exposure dates to the decision in 2021 to finance the reserve itself. The Riksbank held foreign-currency assets against liabilities in kronor. An appreciation reduced the krona value of the assets without reducing the corresponding krona liabilities. When part of the reserve is funded with debt in the same currency, an appreciation reduces the krona value of both that portion of the assets and the matched debt. The central bank has also used FX swaps to hedge currency risk since 2023. It plans to replace those swaps as part of the transition.

The release distinguishes two transactions with different implications for the market. The bank expects to sell some foreign currency for kronor. It also expects to replace an existing hedge. The SEK 200 billion figure covers the borrowing programme as a whole, and the release gives no split between outright sales and swap replacement. An estimate that treated the entire borrowing amount as new purchases of kronor would therefore overstate what can be inferred about outright market demand. The release also gives no currency-by-currency breakdown.

Subject to stable market conditions, the Riksbank provisionally intended to begin in the first quarter of 2027 and complete the change over 12 to 18 months. It planned to spread transactions evenly to limit their effect on the exchange rate. The announced horizon and the two different uses of the proceeds make it impossible to back out a daily spot order from the announced total. The December monetary policy decision was the scheduled occasion for more implementation detail.

The closing section reports reserve assets of about SEK 450 billion at end-October. SEK 200 billion is about 44% of that dated stock, a comparison of scale only. The reserve already had hedges, so the ratio cannot identify the amount of currency risk the operation would remove. The statutory ceiling uses a different denominator. Total foreign-currency borrowing at the decision date may reach 5% of GDP. The reserve still has to provide foreign-currency liquidity for banks, support possible FX intervention and meet Sweden’s obligations under the IMF’s Special Drawing Rights system. Matching asset and liability currencies addresses valuation exposure. Whether assets are readily available when those functions require cash also depends on when the new debt falls due, a schedule the release does not provide.

questions.question: How much of the programme would entail new outright purchases of kronor?
questions.detail: The release identifies outright sales of foreign currency and the replacement of swaps, without quantifying either leg. Compare the Markets Department’s related financing memorandum with the Riksbank’s planned December implementation notice. Track outright transactions and changes in outstanding swaps separately when results become available. For a currency investor, that distinction is necessary before translating the SEK 200 billion borrowing plan into a view on pressure on the krona.

questions.question: Which currencies and dates would concentrate execution risk?
questions.detail: The Riksbank describes an even pace over 12 to 18 months conditional on stable markets. It gives no currency mix or trigger for delaying execution. Compare planned transaction dates with Debt Office borrowing announcements, hedge maturities and currency-specific turnover. An even aggregate pace need not imply an equal daily order in each market, especially if some transactions replace expiring contracts.

questions.question: What liquidity and refinancing risks would remain after currency matching?
questions.detail: The matched debt lowers valuation sensitivity on the funded portion, while the reserve must remain available for contingencies. Compare the currencies and maturities in official reserve disclosures with the Debt Office’s eventual borrowing and redemption schedule. A large payment due during an episode of bank demand for foreign currency could affect immediately usable resources despite limited net exposure to exchange-rate movements.
